title: Prefetch Debottleneck — Weekly alignment and experiment notes
content:
Week: 2026-11-15 to 2026-11-19
Owners: Maya Chen (notes), Liam O'Connor (kernel changes), Priya Desai (benchmarks), Diego Alvarez (canary/infra), Rachel Kim (telemetry)

Purpose: capture alignment from the Thursday runtime sync focused on prefetch and its interactions with KV cache + batching. This is a working doc — rough notes, experimental observations, and action items.

Attendees:
- Maya Chen
- Liam O'Connor
- Priya Desai
- Diego Alvarez
- Rachel Kim
- Guests: SRE on-call (short), Solutions Eng (brief)

High-level summary (one paragraph):
We continue to see tail-latency spikes in long chat sessions under mixed workloads. Our working hypothesis is a mismatch between the prefetch window (how far ahead we fill KV cache/kernels) and the dynamic micro-batching behavior. Kernel-level prefetch is beneficial for steady-state decode but can cause backpressure when many short-inference requests interleave with long ones. This week we ran two micro-experiments (prefetch depth tuning + adaptive-holdback on micro-batches) and instrumented new telemetry to correlate prefetch hits with batch coalescing events. Early results show improved median latency for long sessions at the expense of a small increase in short-request P50 under heavy concurrency — tradeoff needs quantification.

Decisions and direction:
- Short term: land the adaptive prefetch limiter in the canary branch to reduce prefetching when concurrent short requests spike. Rationale: reduce head-of-queue blocking. (Owner: Liam; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/1784)
- Mid term: migrate prefetch heuristics from hard-config to observable-driven policy (telemetry-driven). We will prototype a small controller that consumes prefetched hit rates + batch formation latency and adjusts prefetch depth every 30s. (Owner: Maya/Diego)
- Do NOT change KV cache eviction policy this week; too many confounding variables. Keep experiments limited to prefetch and batching. (All)

Experiments run this week:
1) Prefetch depth sweep (A/B across two dedicated pods)
   - Configs: depth=1,3,6,12 tokens ahead (note: depth is in chunk units rather than tokens in current impl)
   - Metric: median/95/99 latency for long session (seq_len > 1024), short request p50/p95, tail queue time, CPU/GPU utilization, prefetch hit rate
   - Result summary: depth=6 gave best median for long sessions (-18% median), 95th reduced by ~9%. However depth>=6 increased short-request p50 by ~6–10% when concurrency > 120rps due to increased KV lock contention.
   - Takeaway: depth=6 a reasonable default in isolated long workloads; need adaptive controls for mixed workloads.

2) Adaptive-holdback on micro-batches (canary on two nodes)
   - Idea: if a batch contains more than N short requests (<128 tokens) and a long-streaming request is waiting, delay prefetch for that long request until a small grace window to allow micro-batches to drain.
   - Result summary: reduced long-request tail by ~12% in mixed workload tests, but introduced a small increase in overall jitter (std dev latency).
   - Implementation note: introduced a new state (HOLDBACK) in batching state machine; prone to race with in-flight cancellation — we added quick cancel path to avoid stuck requests.

Instrumentation/observability updates:
- Rachel pushed new telemetry tags: prefetch_depth, prefetch_state (IDLE/PREFETCHING/HOLDBACK), kv_lock_wait_ms, microbatch_wait_count. These are on flamegraphs and per-route dashboards.
- New dashboard panels added under Runtime > Prefetch: prefetch_hit_rate (per model variant), avg_kv_lock_wait, prefetch-induced-prefill-duration.
- Linked alert (conservative): fire when kv_lock_wait_ms > 200ms for 5m across >10% of requests (temp threshold while we iterate).

Open issues / unknowns:
- Does prefetch interact poorly with model quantization kernels on A100 -> H100 migration? Priya will run microbenchmarks to confirm kernel-level differences.
- Edge-case: when a prefetch is aborted mid-fill due to model switch fallback, we see stale entries in local prefetch queue; need to ensure cleanup path is robust. (Filed JIRA-RT-885)
- We need a reproducible mixed-workload harness for local dev that mimics PLG traffic (bursty short requests + long sessions). Diego to create a lighter-weight harness in infra.

Action items (ownership + due):
- Liam: finalize and land adaptive prefetch limiter PR (address perf regressions found in canary). Due: 2026-11-23.
- Priya: run kernel microbenchmarks on quantized models across A100 and H100 with prefetch enabled/disabled and report differences. Due: 2026-11-24.
- Diego: stand up mixed-workload harness and CI job (smoke) that runs the harness once/day on canary stack. Due: 2026-11-26.
- Rachel: add prefetch_state to trace context for a 48-hour window and share dashboard link; add sample traces to Confluence. Due: 2026-11-20.
- Maya: draft short doc that describes the adaptive policy design (controller inputs, outputs, safety bounds) for review next sync. Due: 2026-11-22.

Notes to self / meeting fragments:
- "If we over-prefetch, kernel queue becomes the choke point not GPU compute" — Liam
- Diego: "Can we measure prefetch amortization (how many prefetched tokens are actually consumed) per session?" -> useful metric to garbage collect prefetch entries early.
- Bookmark: check related convo in #runtime-prefetch dated 2026-11-12 where solutions eng reported customer case with heavy multiplexing leading to 250ms spikes.

Quick runbook update suggestions (for on-call):
- Add an entry: if kv_lock_wait_ms alert fires, temporarily reduce prefetch_depth on affected node pool via runtime flag and roll pods.
- On-call should escalate to eng-serving-runtime if P99 increases and prefetch_hit_rate < 5% for >10m (sign that prefetch is hurting).

Confluence / PR / Ticket references:
- Confluence doc: CONFLUENCE-3421 (prefetch design notes)
- JIRA: JIRA-RT-885 (bug: prefetch queue stale entries)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/1784 (adaptive prefetch limiter)
- Slack: #runtime-prefetch (search thread "customer multiplexing case")

Next sync agenda (2026-11-26):
- Quick status on PR and canary metrics (Liam, Diego)
- Priya: kernel microbenchmark readout + any quantization interactions
- Rachel: pass/fail criteria for adaptive controller prototype
- Decision point: rollout default prefetch_depth change to 6 for dedicated long-session pools (if no regressions observed)

Unresolved for next week:
- How aggressive should automatic back-off be? (linear vs exponential)
- Whether to expose prefetch controls to customers on Dedicated plans or keep internal only.

End notes: keep experiments small and controlled. Avoid changing eviction policy while testing prefetch. The canary data is promising but noisy; primary focus next week is robust telemetry windows and the harness to reproduce mixed traffic deterministically.

— Maya
